title: What If Every Shark in the Ocean Vanished?

scenes.text: What if every shark vanished? The first thing to disappear would be grass.
In Shark Bay, Australia, tiger sharks keep sea turtles and dugongs out of the shallows where seagrass grows.
Without them, grazers would likely strip the bay bare. Where sharks declined near Bermuda, some seagrass beds nearly vanished.
Seagrass shelters young fish and shellfish that people catch, so fisheries would shrink.
It also stores carbon, so losing it would send carbon dioxide back into the air.
And this isn't far-fetched. Fisheries take around a hundred million sharks a year, and many species have fewer than a dozen young.
